highlights.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
highlights.summary: Jacob Coxon tells the BBC that there's a strong chance AI could end humanity if the rate of development is not reined in.
body: An AI researcher who quit Anthropic told the BBC that people working on the technology are "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.
Jacob Coxon spoke with BBC's Laura Kuenssberg on Saturday about his viral resignation post where he raised concerns about out-of-control artificial intelligence.
"I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," he said.
His resignation comes amid growing safety concerns in the industry, including from his former boss, head of Anthropic Dario Amodei, who in an essay on Saturday argued for development to slow down.

highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
body: As an AI-powered answer engine, Perplexity is deeply focused on search and accuracy. Its ability to process large amounts of information is critically important. Johnny Ho, Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, observes that every time the model gets better at writing code, Perplexity’s search engine improves too. It becomes able to write better programs that search the web and internal information and summarize it very concisely.
But the real challenge, according to Johnny, is taking those informational aspects and applying them to real-world systems. Something made easier with GPT‑6 Astra.
For Johnny, one of the most useful applications of AI is testing code. With limited time to test manually, he asks GPT‑6 Astra to build a small testing program around an application.

The model generates realistic responses like those another service would send, for example, a language model API or a connector. By standing in for those services, the model can check how the application responds and test the workflow from start to finish.

highlights.summary: Elena Rybakina cemented her position as world No 1 by dethroning two-time US Open winner Aryna Sabalenka to seal her maiden title in New York.
body: Rybakina ​won ‌her ​first US Open, beating top seed ‌and defending champion ⁠Sabalenka ​6-4 ​5-7 ⁠6-2 on Arthur Ashe Stadium.
The 27-year-old had already been guaranteed to replace Sabalenka at No 1 in the rankings next week.
Sabalenka was looking to become only the third woman to achieve a New York 'three-peat' in the Open era, after Chris Evert and Serena Williams.
Instead she was left sat in her chair, furiously smashing her racket in to smithereens as Rybakina, from Kazakhstan, celebrated a third Grand Slam title.

highlights.title: Stranger Things Officially Returns Next Week With 10 New Episodes
highlights.summary: Netflix's Stranger Things spinoff Stranger Things: Tales from ’85 will return much sooner than many fans may have guessed. The show’s second season drops on Sept. 17, just a few months after the first season, which aired on April 23.
body: For those unfamiliar with Tales from '85, it’s an animated spin-off of Stranger Thing s set between the main show’s second and third seasons. The series was officially greenlit for a second season shortly after its release. Considering the exceptionally quick turnaround time, it’s probably fair to assume that animation studio Flying Bark Productions was working on the show's next batch of episodes before then.

The first season of Stranger Things: Tales from ’85 received a mixed response from critics and fans, with a 63% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes and a 52% users' score. While some praised the show for recapturing the charm from earlier seasons of Stranger Things, others criticized it as a perfunctory midquel.

Eric Robles and Jennifer Muro developed the show's first season and Robles also served as showrunner. The series' original creators, The Duffer Brothers, were executive producers. It was produced by Netflix Animation Studios, Upside Down Pictures, 21 Laps Entertainment, and Flying Bark Productions. Flying Bark is known for contributing animation to Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, Marvel’s W hat If…?, Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, and more.

highlights.title: September’s Collabs Corner: Raiding John Cena in Clash of Clans, Among Us in Subway Surfers, and more
highlights.summary: Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations. Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places.
body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.

Supercell’s Clash of Clans has formed its second tag team with the WWE, bringing six wrestling stars in-game as playable characters. Among them are Cody Rhodes as Barbarian King, The Undertaker as Grand Warden and Alexa Bliss as Archer Queen.

The collaboration sees players join Cody Rhodes on the hunt for John Cena’s in-game village, unlocking exclusive rewards as they seek out his base this month. The more players raid, the higher the chance of locating the elusive locale. There’s even a Cody Rhodes statue to be found.
John Cena, the wrestling giant turned actor, is said to be a long-time player of Clash of Clans.

highlights.title: Anthony Ippolito on Speaking to Sylvester Stallone Before Filming ‘I Play Rocky’: “Very Overwhelming and Daunting”
highlights.summary: "It was a lot to take in because I'd spent over a year, by that point, studying him,” the actor said at THR‘s Studio at 1 Hotel during TIFF, presented by sponsor Canada Goose.
body: Anthony Ippolito, who stars as a young Sylvester Stallone in I Play Rocky, opened up about speaking with the action star in preparation for the biopic.

Ippolito revealed that he and Stallone chatted about Stallone’s early childhood and many of the difficulties he had to overcome, including paralysis of the lower left side of his face after doctors accidentally severed a nerve during childbirth. The complication gave Stallone his signature voice and look, which became famous when Rocky hit theaters in the ‘70s.

“Since he was born, he had this facial paralysis that kind of made everything difficult,” Ippolito shared. “[The paralysis] obviously made trying to become an actor really difficult. And so, hearing his firsthand account of what that is like; he really just endured a lot and went through a lot. It’s a miracle that this film came to be and that people still celebrate it 50 years later.”
Distributed by United Artists and later MGM, Rocky became one of the most financially successful sports film franchises of all time, grossing over $1.7 billion globally.

highlights.title: I survived a stroke during an ocean swim. Here’s what I’ve learned about fear
highlights.summary: After his stroke in rough surf, Graham Russell embarked on an unexpected journey into fear. Three lessons helped him return to the joy of the ocean. Looking out over the ocean, I would watch the waves sparkling in the sunlight as they grew and spilled into a burst of froth.
body: In winter last year I tore the lining of an artery in my neck during a rough ocean swim off the Central Coast of New South Wales. It caused a stroke while I was in the water, which saw me scrambling back to shore where a surfer noticed me and sounded the alarm. Six months later, the injury had healed, and my motor functions were all back to normal. But as I prepared for a dip in calm conditions on a sunny day in January, I paused. An unexpected journey into fear began.
Standing on the sand, a thousand scenarios would play out in my mind: how big was that wave? Was it powerful enough to injure me? Where would the currents take me? Would I be safe?

I assumed I already knew what fear felt like – I had surfed in rough conditions before, saved lives in the ocean and pursued plenty of adventure in my early years – but this was different. This was fear in the total absence of any bravado or exhilaration or reward. It did not feel like a physical challenge to surmount, it felt simply like my energy would disappear and I would sink beneath the waves.

highlights.title: Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AI
highlights.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says the time has come to slow down AI development and will give third-party evaluators like METR access to its models to help ensure its "adherence to safety practices and commitments." In a winding essay, Amodei proposed a three-step plan to "pace the frontier" - jargon…
body: Dario Amodei proposed a three-step plan to ‘pace the frontier’ of AI development.

Amodei says that giving external evaluators wide-ranging access is just the first step, and one it is taking now unilaterally. Step two would involve the industry coming together as a whole, likely with government agencies to “establish common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” This step would focus on AI companies operating in democratic countries, but because passing laws and building regulatory infrastructure takes time, Amodei says that the industry should work together to create safety standards.

The third step would be the most challenging — getting authoritarian governments like those in China and Russia to agree to slow development and adopt a global set of AI safety standards. But he also says it’s crucial that the US and other democracies maintain a technological lead over China and other authoritarian regimes by limiting their access to high-powered chips and cracking down on things like distillation that allow companies to quickly catch up by training its AI to replicate the behavior of a more powerful model.

highlights.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
highlights.summary: Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.
body: The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

Arsenal had to withstand late pressure from the home side, with Raya saving well from Nordi Mukiele, but they made the result safe when Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty after Reinildo Mandava was shown a second yellow card for hauling him down.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

highlights.title: Diablo 4 On Switch 2: A Very Impressive Port That Supports Mouse Controls
highlights.summary: While Diablo 5 is still on the far-off horizon, a Nintendo Switch 2 port of Diablo 4 is arriving much more imminently. Titled the Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection, it bundles the base game with its expansions Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred for Nintendo's latest system.
body: Polygon went hands-on with the Switch 2 Diablo 4 port at BlizzCon 2026, and confirmed with Blizzard that the port will support Joy-Con 2 mouse controls at launch.

Mouse controls are one of the more unique but underutilized features of the Switch 2. If you place the flat end of a Joy-Con 2 controller down on a surface, you can use mouse cursor-like functionality in games like Fortnite, Metroid Prime 4 Beyond, and Sid Meier's Civilization 7. Considering the PC roots of Diablo as a franchise, mouse control support gives the Switch 2 port a unique feature that you can't find on the other console versions of the game.

Sadly, the Joy-Con 2 controllers at my BlizzCon demo kiosk for Diablo 4: Age of Hatred Collection were locked into the system in handheld mode, so I was not able to try out the mouse controls for myself. Still, I got to try the port in both docked and handheld mode and came away impressed with what I played, albeit with a few caveats.

body: “ I Play Rocky ” held its world premiere Saturday night as part of the festival’s Special Presentations program at the Princess of Wales Theatre. It’s one of the very first movies that has played at the festival that has the potential to win TIFF’s highest honor — the People’s Choice Award. Multiple applauses rang throughout the film as the film recreates the highest points of the 1976 MGM flick that became the highest grossing movie of its respective year, went on to be nominated for 10 Oscars, and winning three including best picture. A post-screening Q&A with Farelly, Ipplolito, Stephan James, Jay Duplass and screenwriter Peter Gamble.

The film chronicles one of Hollywood’s most improbable success stories: a struggling actor with a script nobody wanted and one nonnegotiable demand — that he play the lead himself. As studios dangle money on the condition that an established star throw the punches, Stallone digs in, turning the standoff that follows into its own kind of prizefight.

highlights.title: Elena Rybakina Wins the US Open Women’s Championship
highlights.summary: Elena Rybakina is the freshly crowned US Open women’s champion, beating Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in a closely fought match on Saturday.
body: It’s Rybakina’s third major, having won Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.

It’s Rybakina who came out of the gate faster, stronger, and with fewer errors—serving hard and with pinpoint accuracy, and seemingly bloodless in her power and precision on her way to taking the first set 6-4 (hence her sometime nickname on tour, the “Ice Queen”). Sabalenka’s composure, meanwhile, was maybe best expressed by the warning she received early in the first set for ball abuse after sending one high into the crowd in a moment of frustration.

The two had faced each other 17 times before on the tour, with Sabalenka winning 10 of those matches—but they’d been dead even since 2023. Perhaps more crucially, they’d played each other in two Grand Slam finals (both at the Australian Open), with each player winning once.

highlights.title: Trump is giving data centers a pass to pollute
highlights.summary: President Donald Trump is weakening environmental regulations in the name of speeding up the construction of AI data centers, raising health risks for Americans, a cadre of former EPA officials said this week in a briefing and new report.
body: The Trump administration is sacrificing Americans’ health to build data centers, former EPA officials warn.

At the start of his term, Trump’s EPA administrator, Lee Zeldin, proclaimed his goal of making America “ the AI capital of the world ” through deregulation. Since then, Zeldin and the White House have rolled back dozens of rules on top of cutting staff and funding at the US EPA.

As a result of the Trump administration’s deregulation spree and attacks on renewable energy, the wave of new AI data centers is increasingly powered by dirty energy that can impact Americans’ health even if they don’t live near a data center, the group of EPA alumni warn. They say that the agency they once worked for, which was created to “ protect human health and the environment,” is no longer the watchdog it should be as the physical infrastructure underpinning generative AI changes America’s landscape.
“You would think that an industry buildout of this magnitude, billed as a revolution, would mean more vigilance from EPA.”

highlights.title: 10 Near-Perfect Fantasy Books Recommended by Brandon Sanderson
highlights.summary: Brandon Sanderson is such a prolific author that just getting through his bibliography could keep a reader busy for years. But Sanderson also teaches creative writing and has lectured on the works of J.R.R. Tolkien, often sharing his thoughts on the fantasy genre and its leading talent.
body: Sanderson said that reading Dragonbane in middle school opened his eyes to the power authors had to connect to their readers. Perfect for fans of The Hobbit, Dragonbane unites a prince, a lord, and a witch on a quest to kill a dragon that has taken up residence in the heart of a gnomish cavern. But the mission and the monster are more complicated than they initially seem, offering the potential to harness incredible magic power that could change the fate of the realm.

Melanie Rawn’s debut novel follows Rohan, a prince who finds himself thrust into leadership after his father is wounded by a dragon. The High Prince Roelstra has 17 daughters and no heir, so he sees an opportunity to marry one of the princesses to Rohan and then kill his new son-in-law to steal his lands. Rohan has to play along with the courtship in order to hold onto his new power, but winds up entangled in further schemes with brutal results.

highlights.title: OpenAI IPO will not happen in 2026 amid AI safety fears, Sam Altman says
highlights.summary: OpenAI’s decision comes after dire warnings about rapidly progressing technology and lawmakers’ calls for new rules. OpenAI will not go public in 2026, Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on Saturday, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.
body: “I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don’t feel pressure on that,” Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, told Fortune.

Growing numbers of US lawmakers ​are calling for new rules to govern AI systems after dire warnings from two researchers from OpenAI rival Anthropic that rapidly progressing artificial intelligence could lead to the extinction of the human race ‌in the not-too-distant future.

The warnings follow cases of AI agents going rogue to hack external systems and AI ​safety researchers quitting their companies concerned about the technology’s risks. Politicians, both Democrats and Republicans, have responded with alarm and calls for more action.

The New York Times in June reported that the San Francisco-based OpenAI was considering whether to hold off on a potentially trillion-dollar IPO until next year. At the time, shares in Elon Musk’s SpaceX IPO were tumbling after a surge that sent that company’s valuation to $1.8tn.
points: OpenAI’s decision comes after dire warnings about rapidly progressing technology and lawmakers’ calls for new rules.
OpenAI will not go public in 2026, Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on Saturday, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.
“I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don’t feel pressure on that,” Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, told Fortune.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says it would be ‘ill-advised’ to go public in 2026
highlights.summary: While OpenAI has filed confidentially for an IPO, the company will not be going public this year, according to CEO Sam Altman.
body: Altman was interviewed recently by Fortune editor in chief Alyson Shontell; amidst the fallout from the OpenAI-HuggingFace hack, as well as broader discussions about AI safety, Shontell asked whether OpenAI still feels pressure to “move really fast” due to its IPO plans.
“We’re not rushing into an IPO,” Altman said. “I actually think that given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public.”

Instead, he insisted that OpenAI will go public “when we’re ready, which is when the business is ready, when we feel ready from what the moment is like in society with this technology.” When pressed on whether that means the IPO isn’t happening in 2026, Altman replied, “I would say not 2026, yeah. We’ve got a lot of stuff to do.”

The New York Times reported in June that although OpenAI had hired bankers and lawyers with the goal of going public in the third or fourth quarter of 2026, the company was leaning toward 2027 due to the volatility of tech stocks and its own financial challenges.

If you enjoy the struggle to overcome overwhelming odds, though, it could be right up your alley.

He solves puzzles and completes rhythm-based minigames around the city of Paris, while a twisting caper storyline provides players with ample reason to keep tackling challenges. Sega has a strong heritage when it comes to rhythm games, and this was one of its better ones.

highlights.title: Anthropic CEO outlines plan to slow AI development
highlights.summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman seem to agree that it's time to "pace the frontier." What would that actually look like?
body: We’ve been seeing increasingly dire warnings from AI researchers about the dangers of artificial intelligence, and even comments from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that it may be time to “pace” AI development. But what would that actually look like?

In a new blog post, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei not only echoed the call to “pace the frontier,” but also outlined three broad strategies for doing so. And he said Anthropic is “unilaterally committing” to one of them, with Altman chiming in to say OpenAI will follow suit.

The debate over AI safety and alignment intensified this week after researcher Jacob Coxon wrote that he’s resigning from Anthropic over concerns that the leading AI companies are “gambling with our lives” while the people building the technology “earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” a claim repeated by others at Anthropic.
points: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman seem to agree that it's time to "pace the frontier.

highlights.title: Breville Eye Q toaster review: a ‘revolutionary device’ that makes perfect toast without me trying
highlights.summary: I toasted just about every kind of bread in Breville’s new Eye Q – and each slice came out perfectly toasted. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. It’s a centuries-old problem: how to prepare the perfect slice of toast.
body: The core technology of the toaster has changed little in the past 100 years. A coil of high-resistance wires is activated for a certain period, and the radiant heat from that coil warms and browns the bread. The only measure of doneness that a traditional toaster has is time, but, as anyone who has had burnt toast for breakfast knows, time is a very imprecise proxy.

Breville’s new Eye Q toaster aims to change that legacy. Rather than setting a clock to tick until toast pops out, the Eye Q actually “looks” inside the toaster at the bread to determine whether it is done, thanks to a heat-resistant optical sensor that flashes 10 times per second to monitor the browning process. Hence the gadget’s catch phrase: “We watch your toast so you don’t have to.”

“It took us 10 years to get this project right,” Tom Groundes-Peace, global category manager and head of research at Breville, said. Groundes-Peace likens the innovation to the electric car: while cars evolved over the last century, they were all variations powered by an internal combustion engine. Until the electric motor.

body: Editor’s note: After more than a decade, this is the last WIRED Security News This Week. “The roundup,” as we call it internally, started as a way to ensure that our readers knew about the latest key cybersecurity and privacy news even if we didn’t write about it ourselves. It was a simple way to highlight our own work and the wealth of other great journalism and research published in this realm every week.

Over the years, the roundup has developed a devoted following, and some editions have even become viral hits—which is honestly weird, but the cybersecurity community is great and weird, so it feels right. Rest assured that something new and exciting is coming in the roundup’s place, so stay tuned for that! For now, as always, stay safe out there.

Lawmakers have said they intend to investigate, and the San Francisco City Attorney’s Office ordered the company this week to stop “allowing” AI child abuse ads.

highlights.title: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka to seal dramatic US Open title triumph
highlights.summary: Rybakina wins 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 despite first-serve problems. Overcomes top seed and two-time defending champion. Even when long established as a grand slam champion and a conqueror of all surfaces, Elena Rybakina was always considered lesser than the most successful players of her era.
body: She leaves New York, finally, as the undisputed best tennis player on the planet, the new standard bearer of women’s tennis, after following up her snatching of the No 1 ranking from Aryna Sabalenka by succeeding her as the US Open champion. As she has done throughout this unforgettable week, the Kazakhstani showed her toughness in another spectacular tussle with her great rival, closing out her time at Flushing Meadows with a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory over Sabalenka, the top seed and two-time defending champion.

Before the final, Rybakina had not really played her best tennis this year in New York, but the whole title run stands as the greatest mental performance of her career. She has had to overcome an achilles injury that sidelined her for a week before the tournament and left her uncertain if she would even compete. There was also the potentially suffocating pressure of trying to clinch the world No 1 ranking while being reminded of the exact results required of her to do so. She faced four consecutive grand slam or Olympic champions in the second week of the tournament. She cleared every hurdle without hesitation.

highlights.title: Paramount Leaving California Would Devastate Los Angeles Economy, Leaked Report Finds
highlights.summary: A leaked report from the Los Angeles Economic Development Corporation outlines devastating aftershocks that would follow if David Ellison pulled Paramount Skydance out of California.
body: In August, news broke of Ellison’s plan to take Paramount Skydance out of the Golden State if California Attorney General Rob Bonta and a coalition of other state AGs did not come to the bargaining table and settle their lawsuit to stop the $111 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Ellison gave the AGs until Oct. 1, or he would start packing. The company is considering states such as Georgia, Texas and Tennessee.

The report went on to outline some big-picture stats for if and when Paramount Skydance completed the move: “Once Paramount completed the entire relocation of its headquarters and other operations out of California, the state would experience the permanent loss of approximately 28,990 to 57,980 full-time jobs statewide across all industries, and losses of between $10.6 billion and $21.2 billion annually in economic output.”

On Oct. 1, Paramount Skydance will have to start paying a “ticking fee” to Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders of $7 million a day until the deal closes. The trial between Ellison and the AGs is scheduled to start on March 2, meaning that without a settlement, Paramount is on the hook for about $1.3 billion to WBD shareholders.
